key_insight: A differentiable Schwarz-coupled finite element solver combines near-wall and bulk transport models, enabling inverse modeling of thin boundary layers with agentic AI optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets high-Péclet transport problems where steep near-wall gradients make conventional single-domain simulations and parameter identification computationally demanding.
method: Use perturbation theory to formulate overlapping near-wall and bulk equations, discretized with finite elements.
Enforce governing equations and boundary conditions as hard constraints, with Schwarz coupling enforcing interface continuity.
Use adjoint sensitivities for LLM-guided updates or an AI agent that stages optimization and expands a prescribed functional basis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than nodal fields, but provides no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Agentic optimization benefits may depend on the unknown's representation and the prescribed basis-admission policy.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
